Until now, changing a template meant ope: Until now, changing a template meant opening each contact one by one. Each record keeps its version history, so any of them can be put back.
Until now, deleting a person, a group or:
Until now, deleting a person, a group or a life event by mistake left you with no way back, unless you noticed the undo straight away. Some things, such as an animal, could not be deleted at all.

Now whatever you delete from a vault waits 30 days in its trash, under **Vault settings**, then **Trash**. Restore it and it goes back where it was, with everything deleted at the same time: a person comes back with their relationships, life events and reminders, and a group with its members, notes and files. You can also delete something for good, or empty the trash, before the 30 days are over.
Until now, deleting people or changing t: Until now, deleting people or changing their category meant opening each of them, one after the other. Until now, every vault showed People, Th: Until now, every vault showed People, Things and Knowledge in its sidebar, even the ones you never use. Until now, searching for the label of a: Until now, searching for the label of a phone number, such as “Work” or “Beet farm”, did not find the person it belongs to, and the result showed the number without its label. Now both work again for every contact you save from today.

Each life event shows its date on the left, so its title has the whole line.
Until now, the documentation had a heade: Until now, the documentation had a header of its own, so going from the Monica website to the documentation felt like changing products. Now every page of the documentation opens with the website’s header, with its Features and Docs menus.
Until now, the timeline on the dashboard: Until now, the timeline on the dashboard of a vault opened on Upcoming whenever something was coming up.
